identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log: Toyota 8FGU25 Forklift FL-2 (propane), September 2026, Portland Warehouse
identity.issuer: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC (internal record; header on page 1)

scan.summary: This is your own log of the daily forklift inspections for truck FL-2 in September 2026. It is judged on whether it is complete and up to date. It covers Sep 1 to Sep 18 with day-shift entries only. It has holes: two workdays are missing even though the hour meter shows the truck ran, a horn defect was logged with no record of a repair, there are no entries after Sep 18, and the supervisor review line is blank.
scan.freshness_note: The last entry is Sep 18, 2026, nine days before today (Sep 27). The weekdays Sep 21–25 have no entries. If the truck was used on those days, ask for the rest of the September log or a second page. If they are genuinely missing, record that.

gaps.title: No inspections on Sep 3 and Sep 4 while the truck was running
gaps.description: The log jumps from Sep 2 to Sep 7. The hour meter went from 4,819 to 4,834, about 15 hours, which is roughly two days of use with no inspection recorded. The note at the bottom of page 2 says the same.
gaps.fix: Ask the operators whether inspections were done and not written down. Do not backfill entries. Add a dated note explaining the gap, remind operators that the truck is inspected before use every day it runs, and have a supervisor check the log weekly.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted in Oregon by OAR 437-002-0220
gaps.locator: Page 1, between the Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows; note on page 2
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Horn defect with no record of removal from service or repair
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn was marked X with the note 'Horn not working'. Nothing shows whether the truck was taken out of service, who fixed it, or when. The next entry, on Sep 10, simply shows the horn as OK.
gaps.fix: Find the repair or work order for the horn and file it with this log. From now on, when an item is marked defective, write in the notes that the truck was tagged out, what repair was made, who made it and on what date.

gaps.title: No entries after Sep 18
gaps.description: There are no entries after the Friday, Sep 18 row, although the weekdays Sep 21–25 have already passed.
gaps.fix: Find the entries for Sep 21 onward. If the truck was not used, write that in the log. If it was used without being inspected, record the gap and fix the practice.

gaps.title: Supervisor review not signed
gaps.description: The supervisor review signature and date lines are blank. No rule requires this signature. It is your own form's check, and a signed review would probably have caught the gaps above.
gaps.fix: Have a supervisor review, sign and date the log, and note that the defect and missing days were followed up.
gaps.citation: No specific rule requires a supervisor signature. This is your own form's control.

facts.value: Only day-shift use was recorded for FL-2 in September 2026, so the truck appears to run one shift
facts.affects: On a single shift, a once-daily inspection is enough. Around-the-clock use would need an inspection after each shift.

scan.confidence_notes: The file was clear and every row was read. I am confident about the missing Sep 3–4 entries, the unrepaired horn defect, the blank supervisor line and the last entry date. Whether Sep 21–25 are truly missing depends on whether the truck ran; that finding is inferred from the calendar. Sep 5–6 and Sep 12–13 fall on weekends, and Sep 7 was Labor Day, but the log shows use on Sep 7. The adoption of 29 CFR 1910.178 in Oregon through OAR 437-002-0220 is carried over from the earlier reading and was not re-checked this time.
